summary: Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He founded Thubten Chöling, taught the 14th Dalai Lama and Sogyal Rinpoche, and served as the official head of Nyingma in 2010.

Truman Michelson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard, Leipzig, Bonn, and Columbia under Franz Boas. He worked at Harvard, the University of Missouri, George Washington University (1917–1932), the Bureau of American Ethnology, and the Smithsonian Institution (~1910–1938).
Trung Huynh is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of the West under the doctoral supervision of Darui Long (attested 2016).

Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute and Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp, Thomas Burke, and Khenchen Trinley Paljor Rinpoche, and founded the United Trungram Buddhist Foundation.

Trungram Gyalwa Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Harvard (PhD, 2004). He held visiting positions at the University of Michigan and McGill University (2016).

Tryambak Shankar Shejwalkar was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Mumbai (~1913–1917). He later served on the faculty at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1939–1955).

Tryambakarama Sastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Lakshmana Sastri Dravida at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi, and served as प्रधानाध्यापक at Government Sanskrit Pathashala, Jamnagar (attested 1932).
Tré Khen Zur Lozang Wangchuk studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Trịnh Xuân Thuận is an astrophysicist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the California Institute of Technology, Princeton University, and the University of Virginia, where he also held an academic post starting around 1976.

Tse-fu Kuan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich in 2004. He later held research and academic posts at National Cheng Kung University and Yuan Ze University (attested 2015).

Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Ganden Monastery. He held a post at Ganden Jangtse Monastery and taught the 14th Dalai Lama, Alexander Berzin, Joseph Loizzo, and Thubten Chodron.

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Village, and the University of Glasgow. He served as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Village (~1980–1993) and became Instructor in Tibetan at Oxford in 2001.
Tsering Gyaltsen is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under Dudjom Rinpoche.

Tsering Shakya is a Tibetology and history scholar who earned his BA, MPhil, and PhD from SOAS University of London. He held posts at SOAS (1999–2002), the University of Oxford, and the University of British Columbia (~2007).

Tsewang Gyurme is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He served as President of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and as president of the Tibetan Association for Sacred Studies (attested 2006).

Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Young Lamas Home School. He served at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling (~1976–2020) and Rangjung Yeshe Shenpen (~2003–2020), teaching Andreas Doctor and Phakchok Rinpoche.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Khampagar Monastery and under teachers including Nyoshul Khenpo, Dilgo Khyentse, and Tulku Urgyen. He founded the Pundarika Foundation and held a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

Tsu-lin Mei was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Oberlin College, Harvard University, and Yale University. He held academic posts at Harvard University (~1964–1971) and Cornell University (~1971–2004).

Tsuguhito Takeuchi was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University Bloomington under Christopher I. Beckwith and others. He served as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He held posts at Rissho University, Reiyukai (~1970–1996), the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
